inclusionReview.note: This individually reviewed July 1813 engagement involved Essex, Greenwich and Georgiana and the captures of Charlton, Seringapatam and New Zealander. The inherited 14 July date follows Porter’s narrative sequence (Charles Island on the 12th, departure the next morning, overnight passage and action the following day). NHHC DANFS instead gives 13 July; that one-day disagreement is unresolved and is disclosed here. The conventional Charles Island title is not geographic evidence: Porter places the encounter off Banks Bay after leaving Charles Island. No island centre or unverified offshore point is assigned.

note: Ship numbers cover the whole pursuit and captures, not equal firepower or simultaneous exchanges. Greenwich and Seringapatam fought; the other vessels participated in pursuit, support or surrender. All three British ships were captured, with Charlton later disarmed and released to carry prisoners. Operational removals include capture and do not mean sinking. American ships remained available. Specific hull types, personnel losses, precise offshore position and the one-day 13/14 July disagreement remain unresolved; no people are inferred dead. The inherited 14 July date is retained with the conflicting DANFS date disclosed in the inclusion review.
